learnings.question: Who is credited with the insight that 'a wealth of information creates a poverty of attention'?
learnings.learning: Economist and psychologist Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that an abundance of information necessarily consumes the attention of those receiving it, making attention the scarce resource.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: The saying 'Part of the perfection of one's Islam is his leaving that which does not concern him' is recorded as which numbered hadith in the famous 40 Hadith an-Nawawi collection?
learnings.learning: This hadith, narrated by Abu Hurayrah, is Hadith 12 of the 40 Hadith an-Nawawi collection and teaches that ignoring what doesn't concern you is part of having good, complete Islam.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus proved that we forget about 80% of what we learn within 24 hours unless we actively force ourselves to recall it, which is the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term describes the tendency to forget information simply because we know it has been saved somewhere and can be retrieved later, such as on a phone or computer?
learnings.learning: Researchers call the phenomenon 'Digital Amnesia' or the 'Google Effect': the moment we write something down or store it digitally, our brains treat that as permission to stop holding onto it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact visualizes a Sprint's progress and shows how much work remains, helping the team track whether it's on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is one of Scrum's three artifacts; it visualizes remaining work during a Sprint so the team can see at a glance whether they're on pace to finish.

learnings.question: A common mix-up in Scrum is assuming the Daily Scrum (daily stand-up) is where the team demos finished work to stakeholders. What is the Daily Scrum actually meant for?
options: Reflecting on the Sprint and discussing improvements
Discussing progress, plans, and any blockers
Planning the entire project from start to finish
Demonstrating completed work to the Product Owner
learnings.learning: The Daily Scrum is a short daily meeting focused on progress, plans, and blockers; demoing completed work actually happens at the separate Sprint Review ceremony.

learnings.question: According to Quran 51:56, jinn and humankind were created for what singular purpose?
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 states 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me,' framing worship as the foundational purpose of human and jinn existence.

learnings.question: What Arabic term, used in Quran 2:30, describes humanity's role as caretakers or a successive authority on Earth?
learnings.learning: Quran 2:30 ('Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority') establishes the concept of khalifah: humans as stewards responsible for the Earth and for preserving faith and unity.

learnings.question: Quran 67:2 frames the creation of death and life around which central idea?
options: Testing which person performs the best deeds
Rewarding people for deeds from a past life
Punishing humanity for an original sin
learnings.learning: Quran 67:2, 'He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed,' frames earthly life as a test of conduct whose outcome shapes a person's eternal accountability.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents a device that is fully operational and actively transmitting data, with no power saving applied?
learnings.learning: L0 is the PCIe active state: the device is fully powered on and handling tasks without any power-saving measures, comparable to a computer that's fully on and in use.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state offers the greatest power savings but takes the longest to wake up, comparable to a computer that is completely shut down?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, with the device almost entirely powered down; it delivers the highest power savings at the cost of the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, as distinct from Allah's pre-written, eternal plan?
learnings.learning: Qada' is the actual occurrence of events as they unfold, shaped by a person's own actions and decisions, while Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal knowledge and plan that encompasses even those actions.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: According to a hadith in Jami at-Tirmidhi, what happens when a Muslim sincerely supplicates to Allah for something, as long as it isn't sinful or about severing family ties?
options: The request is automatically granted after 40 repetitions
The request is only granted during the last third of the night
Allah either grants the request or wards off an equivalent amount of evil
Allah only responds to supplications made inside a mosque
learnings.learning: A hadith narrated by Ubadah bin As-Samit (Jami at-Tirmidhi 3573) states that Allah responds to every sincere, permissible supplication either by granting it directly or by turning away an equivalent amount of evil.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: In a word-frequency analysis of the Quran's Arabic text, roughly what percentage of the entire Quran do the 20 most frequently used words account for?
learnings.learning: Testing the Pareto Principle against the Quran's Arabic text showed the top 20 most frequent words accumulate to only about 20.83% of the text, not the 80% the 80/20 rule might suggest.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What is the term for the diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate their vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the small markings added above or below Arabic letters to show which vowel sound to use; without them, written Arabic can be ambiguous since the same spelling can represent different words.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
